title: Denim that actually fits: weight, cut, and why you wash it less
description: Raw denim, fits, and care without the myths. How to spot good jeans, which fabric weight to pick, and how not to wreck them in the first year.
excerpt: Most people buy jeans by the number on the tag. That's exactly why the seat is sagging a month later.
content:
Jeans are the one garment that can last you ten years — and the one most people buy completely blind.

## Weight decides how they age

Denim is measured in ounces per square yard. Under 12 oz is lightweight summer fabric that blows out at the seat fast. 12–14 oz is the all-rounder: holds its shape, comfortable from day one. Above 16 oz you're in raw denim territory — stiff enough to stand on its own for two weeks, then it moulds to your leg exactly. That weight number is the only spec that tells you anything real, and a decent shop lists it.

## Fit is decided sitting down, not standing up

In the fitting room, squat and then sit. If it bites at the crotch or the waistband gapes off your back, that cut isn't yours — and no size change fixes it. Straight and loose fits forgive the most; slim needs the thigh length to be right. Deal with hem length last; a tailor shortens them for pocket change.

## Washing: less often, colder, inside out

It isn't wear that kills denim, it's the machine. Wash inside out at 30 °C, no fabric softener, and only when they actually need it — every ten to fifteen wears is plenty. Skip the dryer entirely; it shrinks seams and eats the colour. Spot-clean a stain with a cloth and cold water immediately instead of running a full cycle.

Solid cuts and raw pairs are at [DOPESTORE](https://dopestore.cz) — and if you keep your own measurements and comparison photos, [FileTools](https://filetools.eu) merges and compresses them into one PDF you can pull up in the shop.

Next time: sit down, check the weight, sort the hem at home. The jeans handle the rest themselves.
